test_checks.description: A plan-change request on a subscription younger than the configured minimum-tenure period is rejected, with no BillingRecord written.
A plan-change request on a SUSPENDED subscription is rejected with a visible reason code and no BillingRecord written.
A preview call returns the computed pro-rata amount without persisting a BillingRecord or changing the subscription's plan.
A commit call on an eligible ACTIVE subscription past minimum tenure updates the subscription's plan and persists a matching BillingRecord.
Two consecutive commits for the same subscription each produce their own independent BillingRecord (no overwrite).
Suspending an ACTIVE subscription transitions it to SUSPENDED and appends a StateTransition.
Resuming a SUSPENDED subscription transitions it back to ACTIVE and appends a StateTransition.

Attempting to suspend a subscription that is not ACTIVE (already SUSPENDED or PENDING_KYC) raises InvalidSubscriberStateException (parametrized over 2 states -> 2 collected items, verified via collect run).
Attempting to resume a subscription that is not SUSPENDED raises InvalidSubscriberStateException (parametrized over 2 states -> 2 collected items, verified via collect run).
Requesting port-out on an ACTIVE subscription transitions it to PORT_OUT_REQUESTED and creates a PortOutEvent.
Cancelling a port-out request within the 7-day window returns the subscription to ACTIVE and closes the event.
Finalizing a port-out request after the 7-day window has elapsed transitions the subscription to PORTED_OUT.
Attempting to finalize a port-out request before the 7-day window has elapsed is rejected.
Requesting port-out on a subscription that is not ACTIVE raises InvalidSubscriberStateException (parametrized over 2 states -> 2 collected items, verified via collect run).

note_for_evaluator: Three backend test names are parametrized (test_suspending_a_non_active_subscription_raises_invalid_state_exception over 2 states, test_resuming_a_non_suspended_subscription_raises_invalid_state_exception over 2 states, test_requesting_port_out_on_a_non_active_subscription_raises_invalid_state_exception over 2 states) — every expected count already accounts for this, verified via pytest --collect-only before writing the contract. Frontend vitest checks (grp-e-06 through grp-e-09) use `-t` name-pattern filtering rather than full test-name selection since vitest's CLI filtering differs from pytest's node-ID syntax — if a `-t` filter matches more or fewer tests than expected, verify the actual vitest test titles in tests/AdminPlanCatalogPage.test.tsx before concluding it's a defect (titles embed their AC tag, e.g. "(AC-2)", by design). A significant NON-CODE finding from this group: no story anywhere builds POST /api/auth/login, yet E1-S4's auth deps and E3-S3's already-evaluated admin router both assume it exists — E2-S4/E3-S4 chose to leave their routes ungated rather than invent unscoped auth wiring, documented in code. This is a spec-decomposition gap, not a contract-evaluation concern for Group E's own ACs (none of which require a login endpoint) — note it in your report but it should not by itself cause a FAIL, since it isn't part of any AC being evaluated here. api_checks/playwright_checks remain empty for the same reason as every prior group (TestClient/vitest equivalent evidence; e2e/admin-plan-catalog.spec.ts exists but is intentionally not run yet — it needs live dev servers and the auth gap resolved first, both out of scope for this evaluation).
